expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
expectations.evidence: Opens: "My recommendation is not to run 8% per cost centre." "8% in every cost centre means about 48 of your 600 jobs go"; "It does not make delivery and compliance shrink as fast as the places with real waste." Paper: "It also cuts equally in the places that earn revenue ..., the places that protect the company ... and the places with real waste."

expectations.text: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
expectations.evidence: "Is the board's real aim a margin, a cash or covenant figure, or opex as such? Does the 8% include restructuring costs?" Paper table maps each aim to its number. Sized: 8% = EUR 5.3m; exit run-rate by Q4 vs budget year; "The honest gap: B leaves about EUR 2.0m (3 points) short in the budget year."

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
expectations.evidence: "Zero-based non-payroll (about EUR 21m): about 10% (range 8-12%). That is EUR 1.7m in-year and EUR 2.1m at run-rate." Outside-opex levers sized: DSO EUR 0.9m cash, rate indexation about EUR 0.8m, utilisation about EUR 0.5m.

expectations.text: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
expectations.evidence: "Hiring freeze: about 47 of roughly 78 expected leavers not replaced ... Exceptions cover roles with signed demand and regulated roles." Paper: "Internal moves first: a vacancy is offered to people on the bench ... Reskill and redeploy"; protected: "training and certification (billable skills), security and compliance, finance controls, customer-facing delivery capacity"; involuntary only after the Q2 gate.

expectations.text: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
expectations.evidence: "Leaders first: 10% pay reduction for about 12 leaders and the profit-linked bonus suspended, EUR 0.5m. Leaders go first"; paper: "leaders take the first and the largest cut".

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
expectations.evidence: Option B table gives amounts by quarter, section 5 gives what stops or waits and the in-year gap (EUR 2.0m) is explicit, but levers have no owner and no confidence rating (only a range on non-payroll and a sensitivity table).

overall_quality.evidence: Honest, well-structured plan with leaders first, a gate and margin levers kept out of the opex number; but the freeze (47 of 78 leavers unreplaced with only 20% assumed billable) is optimistic, levers lack owners, and the reply's 8.3% run-rate includes a year-one-only leaders' cut (7.5% without, disclosed only in the paper).

factual_errors.evidence: (1) "the cohort mix tends to remove younger, cheaper people first": afspiegeling spreads dismissals proportionally across age groups precisely so that younger staff are not removed first; only within each group do the shortest-serving go first. (2) "Cost per exit about EUR 25-40k, payback about 6-12 months at EUR 75k loaded": on its own inputs payback is about 4-6.5 months. Other Dutch points (art. 25 WOR, WMCO before the decision is final, settlements counting, short-time work only for calamities) are correct; Option A and B tables reconcile.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill, reference files or internal jargon such as 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt sets a cost target with a thin but positive margin; no bad outcome is described.

best_insight.value: Keeping margin and cash levers (DSO, rate indexation, utilisation, holding owners' distributions) explicitly outside the opex number so the board is not shown a flattered 8%.
best_insight.evidence: Paper section 4 'Levers outside the opex number (not counted towards the 8%)'.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks whether a 'run-rate' figure includes temporary items (here a one-year leaders' pay cut); that inflates the headline 8.3%.

suggestions.assertion: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples; every reply opened against the flat cut. It does not discriminate. Consider requiring the 'efficient vs wasteful' point to be shown with the user's own numbers or an example.

suggestions.assertion: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten samples. A sharper version would require the no-job levers to be sized in money with a range and shown against the gap, and pricing/leakage kept separate from the opex figure.

No assertion checks in-year versus run-rate phasing of savings and one-off costs under Dutch process (works council advice, WMCO, notice periods). That drove most of the difference in financial soundness between samples.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
suggestions.reason: Compound assertion (amount, timing, owner, confidence, stop list, remaining gap). Several strong samples missed only one element; consider splitting it so partial structure is visible.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong on values and honesty; misses owner and confidence per lever and has two small errors.
